gaps.sentence: He was driving ___ fast for the icy road.
gaps.explanation: 'Too fast for something' means faster than is safe; 'so fast' needs a 'that' clause, not 'for'.

gaps.sentence: ___ students joined the trip this year than last.
There is ___ use asking him — he never checks his messages.
gaps.explanation: 'There is no use doing something' = it is pointless.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: ___ money was spent on advertising last year.
I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.
'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: The hall was so crowded that ___ found a seat.
gaps.hint: a crowded hall means no one succeeded
gaps.explanation: 'So crowded that nobody found a seat' matches the logic of the sentence; 'anybody' cannot be the subject of an affirmative clause.
